incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service affiliates gain entry via edge-device vulnerabilities (firewalls/VPNs), brute force, and stolen credentials, then deploy Go-based encryptors and an EDR-killer framework ('GentleKiller').
incidents.impact: The Gentlemen RaaS operation (offering an unprecedented 90% affiliate payout) has claimed 580 victims across 77 countries since inception, 103 of them in manufacturing; the operators were previously an affiliate of the Qilin RaaS.

incidents.vector: Malware disguised as a portal update was planted on the Balochistan Police complaint-management system, infecting both officers and citizens who used the site.
incidents.impact: A long-running intrusion (Feb 2024-Apr 2026) accessed criminal records, biometric data, personnel files and citizen complaints, assessed as protecting Chinese nationals tied to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor. A separate India-linked espionage group independently breached the same force over the same period.

incidents.victim: Three U.S. organizations (Michigan firm, Oregon tech company, Texas school)
incidents.vector: Network intrusions in 2019-2020 deploying Ryuk ransomware on hundreds of compromised servers and workstations, extorting Bitcoin for decryption keys.
incidents.impact: An Armenian national extradited from Ukraine pleaded guilty to computer fraud and extortion; one Michigan victim paid 200 bitcoin (~$1.1M at the time). He faces up to five years and more than $1.1M in restitution, with sentencing set for September 22.

incidents.vector: A CISA contractor committed privileged Amazon AWS GovCloud keys to a public GitHub repository, exposing them publicly (discovered by a GitGuardian researcher in May).
incidents.impact: CISA took the repo offline, revoked access, and rotated all secrets; log analysis found the leaked credentials were not used outside CISA and no customer or mission data was exposed. A forensic report was released amid congressional scrutiny.

incidents.victim: Ten U.S. companies (nonprofit, financial services, hospitality, healthcare)
incidents.vector: A rogue DigitalMint ransomware negotiator leaked clients' confidential negotiating positions and insurance limits to the BlackCat/AlphV affiliates on the other side of the table, and separately deployed ransomware against additional firms.
incidents.impact: Angelo Martino was sentenced to 70 months in prison for helping extort a combined $75.3M from five clients he was hired to protect (individual ransoms up to ~$26.8M); roughly $10M in assets were seized.

incidents.vector: A Golang backdoor ('GigaWiper') executes on-demand destructive commands — wiping at the physical-disk level, running fake unrecoverable 'ransomware' encryption, and removing partition tables — with persistence disguised as a OneDrive update task.
incidents.impact: Since October 2025 Microsoft has observed environments destructively wiped by this tooling (assembled from earlier ransomware and wiper code), rendering systems irrecoverable while masquerading the destruction as a ransomware event.

incidents.victim: Website owners globally, including many small-to-medium Australian businesses
incidents.vector: Opportunistic mass-scanning exploits dozens of known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (WordPress, Joomla, Craft, and others) to plant webshells on internet-facing web servers.
incidents.impact: Compromised servers give attackers remote control for defacement, credential and data capture, malware distribution to visitors, and a foothold for broader network compromise. Australia's ACSC rates the alert critical and reports many local SMBs already impacted.

incidents.victim: Unpatched Ruckus and ASUS edge routers (used to build proxy infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of known (n-day) vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy a custom multi-platform malware suite and turn the devices into covert relay nodes.
incidents.impact: Actor UAT-7810 is expanding a resilient operational relay box (ORB) proxy network that lets other state groups mask their origins and route traffic through innocuous edge devices, bypassing perimeter defenses against high-value targets.

incidents.victim: Consumers and small/medium businesses in the U.S. and EU
incidents.vector: Malvertising lures victims searching for cracked/pirated software to download password-protected loader archives signed with a fabricated certificate, using file-size inflation and an AMSI bypass to evade sandboxes before dropping an infostealer and cryptominer.
incidents.impact: The Vidar stealer harvests browser credentials, cookies and crypto wallets while XMRig mines Monero; activity spiked in mid-to-late April 2026, sharing infrastructure with a concurrent Lumma stealer campaign.

incidents.vector: A bug in the university's official student app (AMIGO) allowed access to every student's personal data.
incidents.impact: Threat actors could have accessed all students' personal data through the app; the university patched the flaw.

incidents.victim: 2M+ compromised consumer devices (smart TVs, streaming boxes)
incidents.vector: Malicious SDKs bundled into TV-box and smart-TV apps silently conscripted home devices into always-on residential proxy exit nodes rented to third parties.
incidents.impact: Google (GTIG), the FBI, Lumen and others took coordinated action against the NetNut/Popa proxy botnet (estimated 2M+ devices), disabling C2 accounts, sharing SDK intelligence and blocking apps via Play Protect; the disruption significantly degraded the network.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 enterprise mailboxes (finance/AP staff; a U.S. life-sciences company among targets)
incidents.vector: A phishing-as-a-service panel ('ARToken', an EvilTokens variant) abuses Microsoft's OAuth 2.0 device-code grant to steal tokens and bypass MFA, using vendor-impersonation invoice lures and Primary Refresh Token theft for persistence.
incidents.impact: Talos detailed a full affiliate toolkit (80+ API endpoints for email access, BEC and SharePoint exfiltration) sold for $1,500 plus $500/month; recovered lures spoofed a real Wisconsin contractor's accounts-payable to target a U.S. life-sciences firm.

incidents.vector: Customer data theft; intrusion method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole customer data affecting more than 4.38 million customers of Aflac's Japanese life-insurance arm; the company had also disclosed a breach a year earlier.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day vulnerability as part of a wider hacking spree.
incidents.impact: Nissan North America disclosed a security breach linked to the broader Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day campaign.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupting the agency's website and email server.
incidents.impact: DCHA's website and email were disrupted; the agency said scheduled housing payments would not be affected.

incidents.vector: Sustained state-directed cyber operations against Israeli entities.
incidents.impact: Israel's National Cyber Directorate investigated 4,800 incidents in June 2026 versus 1,600 the prior June — roughly triple year-over-year — with most traced to Iran's military and IRGC.

incidents.victim: Transport for London; U.S. healthcare providers SSM Health and Sutter Health
incidents.vector: Voice- and SMS-based phishing to steal employee credentials and MFA codes, SIM-swapping, and network intrusions against corporate systems.
incidents.impact: Two members of the Scattered Spider social-engineering crew pleaded guilty on day one of trial to attacks on Transport for London and U.S. healthcare providers; a related U.S. indictment ties one to broader intrusions and large ransom payments.

incidents.vector: 119 malicious Edge extensions (plus Chrome and Firefox) used steganography to hide command-and-control and deploy payloads three to five days after install.
incidents.impact: The StegoAd extensions stole credentials, backdoored browsers, and ran advertising/search affiliate fraud; Microsoft removed 119 extensions across 90+ developer accounts to disrupt an operation active since at least 2021.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a bug in the platform's web-wallet generation software.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole more than $2.4 million in customer assets; SecondFi paused trading to replace the software and pledged refunds.

incidents.vector: Website defacement.
incidents.impact: Attackers defaced the portal to protest planned internet age-verification laws.

incidents.vector: Alleged digital influence/interference operation run by a private company (named as Israeli firm BlackCore).
incidents.impact: Reports that BlackCore meddled in France's 2026 municipal elections prompted the government to boost funding for its VIGINUM anti-disinformation agency ahead of the presidential election; the claims remain unproven.

incidents.victim: Former Member of the European Parliament (spyware-abuse investigator)
incidents.vector: Repeated Pegasus mobile-spyware infections.
incidents.impact: CitizenLab found the ex-MEP's phone was repeatedly compromised in 2022-2023 while he served on the European Parliament committee investigating spyware abuse; the operator was not attributed.

incidents.victim: 15 major open-source projects (Linux kernel, FFmpeg, 7-Zip, PHP, OpenVPN, VLC and others)
incidents.vector: AI-assisted fuzzing plus manual review produced working exploits, published publicly with no vendor notification.
incidents.impact: A researcher using the pseudonym 'Bikini' disclosed more than a dozen zero-day vulnerabilities with working proof-of-concept exploits (nine assigned CVEs so far), leaving widely used software exposed while vendors scramble to patch; more drops were promised.

incidents.victim: Nidec Corporation (Japanese motor and electronics maker)
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack that forced the company to take its entire IT network offline.
incidents.impact: A newer ransomware group ('BLackField') demanded a $2 million ransom; Nidec was also hit by ransomware in late 2024.

incidents.victim: ~20 technology and SaaS companies via a compromised vendor's Salesforce integrations
incidents.vector: Attackers breached the Klue vendor's network, stole customer OAuth tokens, and used them to reach into customers' Salesforce integrations.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data was stolen from a growing list of nearly 20 downstream companies (including 8x8, BeyondTrust, Deel, Tines, Huntress, Recorded Future and Snyk) through the compromised integrations.

incidents.vector: Network breach and data-extortion; 200,000 documents leaked after the supplier refused to pay.
incidents.impact: Images of the upcoming iPhone 18 (battery, chips, circuit boards) leaked after the World Leaks group exfiltrated and published 200,000 documents.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and data theft roughly three weeks before the stolen files were leaked.
incidents.impact: Files allegedly taken from the central bank were leaked on the dark web by the Qilin ransomware group; Libyan authorities are investigating.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion and extortion by a newly-launched operation ('Settra').
incidents.impact: One of Taiwan's largest mobile operators was hacked and extorted; the telco says its mobile-payments platform was unaffected and the Ministry of Digital Affairs opened an investigation.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into a cloud-based platform, consistent with exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft in the wider spree.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed patient data and internal documents; AdaptHealth notified the SEC and investors and appears to be a victim of the broader Oracle PeopleSoft campaign.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security — Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN)
incidents.vector: Intrusion targeting HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system.
incidents.impact: Attackers breached a DHS network used to share sensitive data with federal, state, local and industry partners between late May and early June; the intruders and data taken remain unknown.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion by the ShinyHunters data-extortion group at the start of June.
incidents.impact: NAIC suspended insurer risk designations and some credit-rating agencies paused data sharing; the association says it has since evicted the intruders and is restoring operations.

incidents.victim: Latvijas Valsts Meži (LVM), Latvia's state-owned forestry company
incidents.vector: Exploited a system that had not been updated for two years; attackers dwelled in the network over a week before detection.
incidents.impact: Mapping, hunting and contractor systems were knocked offline and data leaked; weeks after the attack the company was still restoring systems, with many contract customers still without access. Election infrastructure was confirmed unaffected.

incidents.vector: Network breach and data-theft extortion by the Silent Ransom Group.
incidents.impact: The law firm was breached in May and refused to pay the ransom.

incidents.vector: Destructive intrusion wiping servers, workstations and virtual machines and deleting backups.
incidents.impact: The Cyber Anarchy Squad claims to have wiped 3,000 servers/workstations and 700 VMs, deleted all backups, and stolen more than 650 TB of documents.

incidents.vector: Network breach; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: A breach between March and April exposed employee information; no group has claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on a central healthcare service provider that services 95% of Germany's university hospitals and over half of large clinics.
incidents.impact: Tens of thousands of patients' sensitive health data were stolen; the incident illustrates how compromising one provider can reach many hospitals.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack forcing shutdown of network access across the medical center's facilities.
incidents.impact: The February attack disrupted operations for more than two weeks across UMMC's facilities.

incidents.vector: Data breach at a healthcare service provider; details not specified.
incidents.impact: The provider disclosed a data breach affecting 3.4 million patients at its customers' facilities.

incidents.vector: A Dutch-speaking accomplice posing as an Odido IT employee phoned customer service (vishing) to trick staff into granting access to a customer contact system, enabling bulk download of records.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 6 million customers was exposed; Dutch police traced the attack to a suspected local accomplice and continue to investigate.

incidents.vector: Data breach originating in December; details not specified.
incidents.impact: The company revealed a December breach affecting 3.1 million people.
